title: Remote environments: follow-ups from #2087 (#2050, D510)
body:
Non-blocking follow-ups the independent security review of #2087 recorded (none weakens what #2087 adds; each is stricter-or-equal to main):

1. **Check-then-use gap.** #2087 asks the executor for its sandbox report (`environment/info`) before each command round and each remote file operation, with no cache. If a different executor answers behind the same URL between the check and the use, only requests that carry a sandbox are re-checked on the executor side. Unsandboxed launches (Permissive full access; nothing at Moderate/Aggressive) and the "elevated asked for but not set up" file case have no executor-side re-check. Option: mark such requests so a new executor refuses them itself when it has no sandbox.
2. **Capability-root discovery** (skill/plugin manifests, `session/mcp.rs`) and skill resource reads with `sandbox: None` never carry the refusal. The same is true locally under D491 (#1976).
3. **PF-27-S06** in `core/src/tools/runtimes/apply_patch.rs` decides whether a sandbox can deny reads with the client's `cfg!(windows)`, so a Mac client patching on a remote Windows executor takes the non-Windows branch. This predates #2087.
4. **Startup notice:** there is no notice for a remote Windows environment without a sandbox (the local case has one, #1976). The refusal explains itself at first use.
5. **Performance:** each command round and each remote file operation adds one `environment/info` call (up to its 30 s timeout). A short per-connection cache would help without weakening the fail-closed behaviour.
6. **Typing edge case:** typing into a remote process is judged against the executor's current report at the level the process started with. A process started with `Elevated` before the remote setup finished counts as confined once the setup completes.

Related: #2050, #2049, #1976, #2003, #2009.

— Corbanu Terminal maintainers
